en: The Devatādhyāya Brāhmaṇa, First Section:
Agni, Indra, Prajāpati, Soma, Varuṇa, Tvaṣṭṛ, the Aṅgirases, Pūṣan, Sarasvatī, and Indra-Agni. 1.
Those whose finales are *iḍā*, those whose finales are *pada*, and those whose finales are *ikāra* belong to Agni. || 2 ||
All [the verses] ending in *nidhana* belong to Indra, except for those that have been specifically assigned. 3.
All the *svāra* chants belong to Prajāpati. 4.
Or as the Vāmadevya [sāman]. 5.
The Ṛgveda verses, the Sāman chants, and the Yajus formulas. 6.
As in the case of *auśanaka* and *auśana*. 7.
The Vāṅnidhana chants belong to Varuṇa. 8.
Just as in the case of the Yajñāyajñīya [sāman]. 9.
The syllables and vowels belong to Tvaṣṭṛ;
as, for example, the Vāravantīya and the Ābhīvarta. || 10–11 ||
The *svaḥpṛṣṭha* hymns belong to the Aṅgirases. 12.
The Pauṣa months possess excellent wealth. 13.
"By what means shall he come to us wondrously? Flow forth [the wealth] consisting of thousands"—this is for the Sarasvatī sacrifice with the *vāṅnidhana*.
"Ya ānayat parāvataḥ"—this [verse] is for Indra and Agni. || 15 ||
"Established in wealth, power established in wealth"—with these two verses dedicated to Agni and Indra [he should worship]. || 16 ||
The Vasus, the Rudras, the Ādityas, and the Viśvedevas. 17.

The *svāra* chants belong to the Vasus; those with the *nidhana* [ending] belong to the Rudras; those with the *aiḍa* [chant] belong to the Ādityas; and those with the *vāṅnidhana* [ending] belong to the Viśvedevas. || 18 ||
Just as regions exist by virtue of their greater extent, so too are the intermediate spaces [defined]. 19.

Now, as for the more intimate [Sāmans]: all those dedicated to Agni, all those dedicated to Indra, all those dedicated to Svar, and all those dedicated to Prajāpati—these are the more intimate [Sāmans]. || 20 ||
Now, all the Brāhmaṇa Sāmans are the most similar; thus they are the most similar of all. 21.
Now follows the Upaniṣad. 22.
The Ṛgveda is the mother, the Sāmaveda is the father, and Prajāpati is the tone.

Now, those which are explained according to the *ṛc* are explained from the mother; those which are explained according to the *sāman* are explained from the father; and those which are explained according to the accent (*svara*) are explained from Prajāpati. 24.
This very Udgītha is possessed of kin; it belongs to those who possess kin.
Thus ends the first section in the fifth Brāhmaṇa of the Devatādhyāya in the Vedārthaprakāśa. || 1 ||
The second section:
Now, therefore, follow the syllable-counts of the meters. 1.

The Gāyatrīs are white by form; the Uṣṇih verses have the form of a dappled deer; the Kakubhs are tawny in form; thereafter, the Anuṣṭubhs are black. The Bṛhatīs are red, while the Paṅktis are blue; furthermore, the Triṣṭubhs are golden in form, and the Jagatīs are said to be fair.

Therefore, among the other meters, Śyāva is their [lord]; from him, again, Nakula is the lord of the one-footed meters, while Babhru is said to be the lord of the two-footed. Those possessing the forms of Sāraṅga, white, and black are associated with the Ṛg, Yajus, Sāman, and Brāhmaṇas. (3)
Those [mantras] which are to be employed in sacrifices—their presiding deity is now being declared. (4)
One should know the variegated speckled ones as Virāj. || 5 ||
The deity is superior even to that. || 6 ||
The Gāyatrī became the companion of Agni; Savitṛ was united with the Uṣṇih; Soma, great through hymns, was joined with the Anuṣṭubh; and the Bṛhatī protected the speech of Bṛhaspati. 7.

The Virāj belongs to Mitra and Varuṇa; the Abhiśrī is the portion of Indra; the Triṣṭubh entered here as the share of the day; the Jagatī has entered all the gods; by that the seers among men were fashioned. 8.

The Aticchandas and Vicchandas meters have Prajāpati as their deity and Vāyu as their presiding divinity; among bipeds, the Puruṣa is the deity, and the Ekapadās are remembered as having Brāhmī as their deity. || 9 ||
The Vāsavī metre consists of ten syllables.
One should consider this as being with a *tuṣṇīm* (silent) [verse]; for in these meters, the *ṛc*s are indeed addressed to those very deities. || 11 ||
This, indeed, is the deity of the Vedic hymns.
Thus ends the second section in the fifth Brāhmaṇa of the Devatādhyāya in the Vedārthaprakāśa.
The third section:
Now, therefore, the etymological explanation. 1.
Gāyatrī [is so called] from the root *gai*, meaning "to praise. 2.
"For it fell from the mouth of him who was singing," so says the Brāhmaṇa.
The term *uṣṇīṣiṇī* is derived from the root *uṣ* (to burn) with the suffix *niṣ*, or from the root *sṛh* (to love/beauty), meaning "possessing beauty"; thus it is a metaphorical designation. 4.
"Kakup" means "having the form of a hump"; this is a metaphorical expression. 5.
And *kakub* and *kubja* [are derived] from the root *kuja*, meaning "to bend. 6.
The *anuṣṭubh* [is so called] because of its praising (*anu-stobhana*). 7.
"For he praised [them]," so says the Brāhmaṇa. || 8 ||
The word *pipīlikā* [is derived] from the verbal root *pela*, which has the sense of "going. 9.
The "ant-middle" is an illustrative simile. 10.
*Bṛhatī* is derived from the root *bṛh*, meaning "to increase. (11)
He is called Virāj because of his cessation from passion, because of his shining forth, or because of his transcending [all things]. || 12 ||
The *paṅkti* consists of five [syllables], has five lines, and contains five feet. 13.
The *triṣṭubh* chants with the subsequent word as its *stobha*. 14.
"But which one would be the Tritā? It is the metre that has crossed over the most," he said. || 15 ||
"The threefold vajra, its 'stobhinī' [is like that]"—this is a simile. (16)
The *jagatī* is the most pervasive of meters; that which is *jagatī* possesses swift movement. (17)
"He created [them] while making them tattered," for such is the Brāhmaṇa.
The word *aticchanda* is used in the sense of *chada* (covering). 19.
The *chandāṃsi* (Vedic meters) are so called because they delight (*chandayati*). 20.
The *nicṛt* [meter] is derived from the root *cṛt* preceded by the prefix *ni*; it is called *bhurik* because of its supporting (*bharaṇa*) [the syllables]. || 21 ||
Now, therefore, the Gāyatra-sāman dedicated to Agni arises through its constituent parts; it is the Sāman of the gods, or of the ancient seers, or of Parameṣṭhin, the son of Prajāpati. 22.
Where the Sāvitrī-geya has not been sung. || 23 ||

He who knows the domain of the seers is liberated from the body; having transcended the further shore of darkness, he is glorified in the heavenly world. That which is called a day of Brahmā, lasting for a thousand yugas—at the end of that time, he shines in heaven like the sun upon the back of the firmament. Then, at the beginning of the Kṛta Yuga, the highly illustrious, all-knowing, and steadfast seer, having become one with Brahman, is born again with full recollection. Thus [it is said]. "With recollection"—this refers to verse 24.
Thus ends the third section in the fifth Brāhmaṇa of the Devatādhyāya in the Vedārthaprakāśa. 3.

The Fourth Section: Now we shall explain the limbs of the Sāvitrī. Brahmā is the head; the sky is the forehead; the moon and sun are the eyes; Agni is the mouth; Sarasvatī is the tongue; Tvaṣṭṛ is the neck; the Vasus are the arms; Vāyu is the chest; the Pāyavas are the body hairs; Indra is the back; Viṣṇu is the navel; Prajāpati is the belly; the Maruts are the thighs; the Vedas are the feet; the lightning is the smile; the wind is the breath; the mountains are the bones; the oceans are the garments; and the stars are the ornaments. 1.
Whoever knows thus. || 2 ||
May there be well-being from everything that is corrupted, improperly applied, deficient, or excessive. 3.
May there be well-being for the divine sages. 4.
May Brahman and Truth protect me! May Brahman and Truth protect me! (5)
Thus ends the fourth section in the fifth Brāhmaṇa of the Devatādhyāya in the Vedārthaprakāśa. 3.
The Brahmaṇa on the Deities is completed.
